newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA OTC MARKET INCHES DOWN, REBOUND PREDICTED.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA OTC MARKET INCHES DOWN, REBOUND PREDICTED.

text.p: Romania's over-the-counter (OTC) market inched down on Wednesday in thin buying interest in the holiday season, traders said.
"Interest stayed light throughout the day, although the prices of several small-caps are rather attractive," one trader said.
Operators forecast the market would remain subdued until the end of the month. Early September is expected to bring the market in a bullish phase.
Three independent market indices slipped on Wednesday.
The VAB-RA all-share index inched down by 1.7 percent to 6,336.2 points, the BIG-OTC eased 1.14 percent to 4,544.24 points. The CAS-RQ lost 0.98 percent to 990 points.
Losers outnumbered winers by 193 to 175, while the prices of 277 stocks were unchanged.
Operators said they expected the market to pick up after new rules on Wednesday by Romania's central bank to regulate repatriation in foreign investment come into force.
"The norms will help to boost confidence in the local market," a trader said.

Acording the new procedures, non-residents acting as foreign investors are given access to the local foreign exchange market where they can submit spot or forward hard currency buying and selling orders related to their investments in Romania.
The norms have to be published in the Official Gazette to become effective.

Wednesday's losers included cement maker Romcim, which softened 2000 lei to 120,000 lei, despite an announcement that its main stockholder would start negotiating sale of 51 percent with five bidders for the stake.
"The market will react probably only when the successful bidder is announced," a broker said.
Arpechim oil refinery lost 1,000 lei in late trade and closed at 39,000, while Petromidia, another refinery, went up 500 lei to 43,000.
Ball bearing makers continued to slip under selling pressure. Rulmenti Brasov lost 100 lei to close at 1,100.
